newsitem.title: UK: NWE straight-run fuel oil ends week unchanged.
newsitem.headline: NWE straight-run fuel oil ends week unchanged.

text.p: European low sulphur straight-run ended the week unchanged with no deals done after a seller was heard to have decided to move a cargo it was marketing into its own system.

Traders said the seller, a Norwegian major, has decided to take the July 5-10 30,000 tonne loader into their own system after no agreement was reached with a potential buyer, an independent U.S. refiner.
The seller was heard to be sticking to its $103 fob asking price but the buyer, who moved to $102, went back down nearer to the $100 mark after crude futures fell late on Thursday.
Traders said the main obstacle to concluding the deal was operational problems over the loading date.
A second seller said it was not marketing its end month cargo but said it would do $104/$105 at present.
"In June when crude was at $18 were were talking $104/$105 so I don't think that that is too high a price to ask. But I am not actively marketing," the trader said.
